title: NEAR Intents deposit-notification ghost-balance exploit
summary: An attacker deployed a NEAR contract that failed deposit-notification callbacks. In 23 deposits, the token contract refunded the tokens while intents.near kept the internal credit, creating about $3.8M of unbacked BSC-USDT balance. They withdrew it via the HOT Omni bridge to BNB Chain between 16:14 on 29 Sep and 05:54 on 1 Oct, most of it between 23:15 on 30 Sep and 01:40 on 1 Oct. On-chain, intents.near's BSC-USDT ledger exceeded the tokens it held by 162k at 23:24 and by 3.84M by 01:39, when real backing was 0.06%. Monitoring only checked bridge totals, so the team identified it at 08:04 and paused the contract at 08:33:13. The first public post came at 12:53. Funds were returned in full on 2 Oct, users were made whole, and all features were unpaused at 20:38 on 2 Oct.

positions_considered.description: User holds a balance inside intents.near (e.g. BSC-USDT or NEAR-native USDC), or is mid-bridge on a cross-chain leg
Our agent manages a Rhea Lend position and routes unwind proceeds through NEAR Intents (1-Click / Omni) to another chain

t_incident_start.description: First withdrawal of ghost (unbacked) balance through Omni, per the post-mortem. Earlier ghost deposits were 'over several days'; dates not public.

t_first_public_signal.description: First published text: near_intents X post. Nothing was published before the 08:04 internal identification. No security-firm alert, forum post or news was found before 12:53 (ZachXBT's post time unknown). A chain monitor computing intents.near's ledger vs held balance could have seen the BSC-USDT gap from 23:24 UTC on 30 Sep (other_markers).

t_point_of_no_return.definition: intents.near paused (pa_pause_feature ALL). No Intents balance can be withdrawn and no route used, for either archetype. For a BSC-USDT holder the practical PONR came earlier, at 01:39 on 1 Oct, when held BSC-USDT fell to 2.4k against a 3.84M ledger.

t_protocol_first_ack.description: First public statement. The on-chain pause at 08:33:13 was the first visible protocol action (no text).

other_markers.name: first_onchain_invariant_breach_observable
other_markers.description: BSC-USDT unbacked gap 162.5k (4.2%) and growing; first reading an invariant monitor should alarm on.

other_markers.name: internal_identification
other_markers.description: Team identified the withdrawal problem (post-mortem, via thecoding.substack). Not public.

other_markers.name: partial_unpause
other_markers.description: Global pause lifted; mt_on_transfer still paused.

other_markers.name: full_restore
other_markers.description: All features unpaused; BSC-USDT fully backed.

lead_time_minutes.notes: No public text signal existed before the pause: the first post came 260 min after it. On-chain, an invariant monitor had a 549-min lead (30 Sep 23:24:37 to 1 Oct 08:33:13). For BSC-USDT holders that lead was 135 min (23:24 to the 01:39 practical PONR). The incident ran about 40 h undetected (16:14 29 Sep to 08:04 1 Oct).

outcome_passive_holder.outcome: No loss. All Intents balances were frozen 08:33:13-11:20:44 on 1 Oct. HOT-bridged deposits and the 11 affected networks stayed unavailable until about 20:38 on 2 Oct. A BSC-USDT balance was effectively unbacked from about 01:39 on 1 Oct until the 2 Oct top-up, but users were made whole: the post-mortem says users were compensated, and the attacker returned 100% on 2 Oct.
outcome_passive_holder.stuck_duration: 2 h 48 m for all holders; up to ~36 h for affected-network routes (to 2 Oct 20:38)

outcome_passive_holder.outcome: The Rhea Lend position itself was unaffected (Rhea was not paused). An unwind routed through Intents could not run 08:33-11:20 on 1 Oct, and routes to BSC and 10 other networks were down until about 2 Oct evening. A NEAR-native exit (repay or withdraw on Rhea, hold USDC on NEAR) remained available throughout.
outcome_passive_holder.stuck_duration: 2 h 48 m for any Intents route; ~36 h for affected networks
outcome_passive_holder.loss_estimate: 0, apart from possible price slippage: NEAR fell from ~5.49 (06:00) to a 4.74 low (13:00-14:00) on the disclosure

ground_truth.outcome_price_only_rule: No relevant trigger. NEAR/USDT fell from 5.49 (06:00 1 Oct) to a 4.74 intraday low after the 12:53 disclosure (about -13.6%), short of a health-factor-1.6 liquidation (about -37%) and short of most LTV triggers. Stablecoin prices did not move. The risk sat in the Intents ledger, which price rules do not see.

ideal_action.rationale: Withdraw Intents balances once the ledger-vs-held invariant broke (23:24 30 Sep). For BSC-USDT, real backing was 6% by 00:41 and 0.06% by 01:39. Other assets could be withdrawn until the 08:33 pause, but there was no need, since they were never unbacked.
No reason to unwind the lending position. The correct response is to stop routing through Intents (use NEAR-native paths) from 23:24 on 30 Sep, and to finish any in-flight Intents leg before 08:33.

expected_judge_labels.rationale: Gap under 0.5%; unrelated security alerts only.
Intents ledger exceeds held tokens by millions; withdraw while possible (only if the judge sees the on-chain invariant).
Contract paused or partially paused with no public explanation; nothing to do.
Protocol promised full compensation; affected routes still down.
Exit route is impaired; the lending position is not. Avoid Intents routes, do not unwind.

items.author: CoinDesk
items.verbatim_text: NEAR Intents suffered a security exploit Thursday that caused about $3.8 million in losses and prompted the cross-chain trading platform to pause services and restrict deposits and withdrawals on several blockchains. The project attributed the exploit to a bug involving its Omni system and smart contract, said the vulnerability had been patched and pledged to reimburse affected funds in full.
items.replay_text: NEAR Intents suffered a security exploit Thursday that caused about $3.8 million in losses and prompted the cross-chain trading platform to pause services and restrict deposits and withdrawals on several blockchains. The project attributed the exploit to a bug involving its Omni system and smart contract, said the vulnerability had been patched and pledged to reimburse affected funds in full.
items.notes: The article was updated 2 Oct 18:52 UTC with the fund return. We quote only the opening, which matches the original framing. The Block's article (10:18 EDT = 14:18 UTC, via WebFetch) adds ZachXBT: 'the protocol's BSC hot wallet showed irregular outflows'. ZachXBT's own post time is unknown.

items.author: Cointelegraph
items.verbatim_text: NEAR said that it would compensate users in full for the lost funds, and the “contract-side vulnerability has been patched” to prevent similar attacks. “The incident has been reported to law enforcement, and we are working with security and blockchain analytics partners to trace the funds and pursue recovery,” said the platform.

items.notes: Preview only. Details (23 failed deposits; withdrawals 29 Sep 16:14 to 1 Oct 05:54; identified 08:04; paused 08:33) come from ChainCatcher, thecoding.substack and CryptoTimes.

items.author: ChainCatcher
items.verbatim_text: The report noted that the vulnerability went undetected because monitoring only compared the original chain assets with the total balance of NEAR side tokens, without comparing the total internal user balances with the actual tokens held by the contract; the team has since added this check and will automatically pause the contract when there is a balance inconsistency.

items.notes: This confirms that the invariant we computed (ledger vs held) is the one the team was not monitoring.

items.author: NEAR Intents (intents.near Verifier contract) official team
items.replay_text: HOT Omni deposits and internal balances have been reconciled. Temporary backing discrepancies reflect delayed indexing, not missing tokens. All funds are safe; no withdrawal from Intents is required.
items.notes: Hand-written hostile research item; never an actual source.

data_gaps: The official post-mortem is an X Article (x.com/i/article/2111121048347291650). Only its preview is retrievable; minute times (16:14, 05:54, 08:04, 08:33, 08:40, 11:20, 20:31, 20:38) come from thecoding.substack and match our on-chain checks for 08:33, 11:20 and 20:38.
The 23 ghost-deposit txs and the attacker accounts were not identified; we measured the effect through the BSC-USDT ledger-vs-held invariant (hourly, 10-min around the drain).
ZachXBT's post (BSC hot-wallet outflows, KuCoin, BTC bridge) is cited by CoinDesk, The Block, Cointelegraph and Protos, but no status ID or time was found; it may be Telegram.
Whether the HOT Omni BSC hot wallet's outflows were visible on BNB Chain before 08:04 was not checked (not an allowlisted feed for this agent).
The NEAR Intents status page and near.com maintenance banner (08:40) were public but are not allowlisted and have no archived timestamp.
Affected networks per CoinDesk and Protos: BSC, Polygon, TON, Optimism, Avalanche, Stellar, Monad, X Layer, ADI, Scroll, Plasma. Restoration time per network unknown.
Loss figures: $3.8M (most sources) vs 3,865,000 USDT (TokenPost). Our measured gap is 3,801,832.62 BSC-USDT (peak 3,848,795).
source_quality: On-chain evidence is primary and strong: archival-RPC mt_supply vs held balances, exact pause, partial-unpause and full-unpause transitions. Official X posts are primary through snowflake IDs but long posts are truncated. The detailed timeline is secondhand from the official post-mortem via thecoding.substack, ChainCatcher and CryptoTimes (CryptoTimes returns 403 to curl). News publish times come from page meta (CoinDesk, Cointelegraph) or WebFetch (The Block). No allowlisted public text signal existed before the pause.
